spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The search first subtracts what the Gram block already guarantees, leaving a localized deficit of two sign changes. It then spends evaluations in an evidence-ranked order: likelier outer interval, other outer interval, and finally a broader length-dependent fallback.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For a Gram block of length L at least two, the source says L-2 sign changes have already been detected implicitly, so the remaining task is to find two changes that, if present, lie in one Gram interval. Preliminary experiments place them usually in an outer interval. The program chooses between the outer intervals using the smaller absolute sum of endpoint Z-values, uses parabolic interpolation, then tries the other outer interval and a whole-block or interior fallback according to L.
directed.conceptual_reading: This is a deficit-and-localization strategy: use structural accounting to reduce the objective, a cheap endpoint proxy to rank candidate regions, and progressively broader search only after cheap likely cases fail. The ordering is empirical and cost-aware rather than deductively forced.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Gram-block boundaries turn a global zero-separation task into interval-local subproblems. Endpoint values of Z supply the ranking proxy, while parabolic interpolation bridges sampled values to candidate interior sign behavior; the final fallback delegates details to an earlier routine and program source.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The outer-first rule is not a theorem that missing changes are outermost, and the source qualifies their existence. Exact subscripts and the displayed comparison are OCR-garbled, so symbolic reuse needs the scan. Termination without finding the pair triggers a separate failure path rather than validating the block.
directed.uncertainty: High confidence in the prose-described staged strategy and missing-two reduction; moderate confidence in exact endpoint notation because of OCR damage.

supported: The L-minus-two accounting, localization of the missing pair to one interval, outer-interval priority, endpoint-value ranking, parabolic interpolation, second outer interval, and length-dependent fallback are all supported.
The candidate correctly treats outer-first as empirical and conditional rather than deductive.
inference: Deficit-and-localization and progressive broadening are faithful strategic abstractions of the staged search.
Calling the endpoint expression a cheap proxy and interpolation a bridge to interior behavior is interpretive but grounded.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The program deliberately separates throughput from certification: unresolved blocks are allowed to pass provisionally only because a message and plot preserve them for later human inspection, after which an overrun beyond the target and a cited theorem close the finite claim.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: If an automated search finds the missing two sign changes, computation advances to a new block. Otherwise it emits a message and a plot of Z over the block, proceeds provisionally as if the changes were found, and subjects such plots to later manual inspection, including adjacent blocks. After computing slightly beyond the target range and finding four further blocks satisfying Rosser's rule, the authors invoke Theorem 3.2 of Brent to complete their finite zero claim.
directed.conceptual_reading: Exceptional cases are converted into durable audit objects instead of being silently conflated with successful automatic cases. The extra range acts as boundary context, while the cited theorem is the logical bridge from local sign evidence to the announced prefix statement.
directed.representation_or_bridge: A plotted Z-profile makes an unresolved numerical trajectory inspectable across a whole Gram block and its neighbors. The separate theorem, not the plot alone, connects the completed sign-change record and the overrun to the claimed count of simple critical-line zeros.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Pretending that the changes were found is unsafe without the preserved exception and later inspection. The span does not formalize the manual judgments and does not reproduce Theorem 3.2, so its final implication cannot be independently reconstructed here. The conclusion remains a finite computation, not RH.
directed.uncertainty: High confidence in the failure-handling workflow; the exact zero count and formula symbols are OCR-risky, and the final closure is dependent on an external cited theorem.

unit_result_entry.title: Shifted sampling can change the observed class of a Rosser-rule exception
unit_result_entry.why_material: The source warns that shifted Gram-point evaluation may miss or reclassify exceptions, gives a concrete zero-pattern mechanism for such reclassification, and distinguishes six exception types while noting that one type had not been observed.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Small argument shifts reduce expensive fallbacks but break strict count accumulation
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: When method A cannot rigorously determine a sign, the program tries small shifts before invoking method B. This optimization means some evaluations occur near rather than exactly at Gram points, so its statistics are not strictly accumulable with Brent's even though the paper presents them together.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Selected subranges can efficiently screen for Rosser-rule exceptions
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: A different method searches only selected small ranges inside a height interval and nevertheless recovers all exceptions in one comparison range and most in another, showing that rare-event detection need not exhaustively scan the whole interval in the same way.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Argument shifts and selective-range screening reduce computational effort but can change detection or classification of rare exceptions, so cross-program overlap checks and explicit sampling provenance are part of the evidential method rather than incidental bookkeeping.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The overlap comparisons are bounded to stated ranges, and the source does not provide the construction of the alternative selected ranges.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Optimization of observations can alter the measured exception process

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The exception taxonomy is partly observer-dependent: moving the sampling points can make the same local zero arrangement appear as a different Gram-block pattern, so overlap agreement and explicit detection caveats are necessary alongside the exception list.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source lists exceptions to Rosser's rule and warns that shifts at Gram points may have caused some to be missed. It gives a mechanism: an exception called type 2 under the exact convention may be detected as a length-three block with zero pattern 2-1-0. On one overlapping range the L R and W program found the same exceptions as Brent. The authors extend the taxonomy to six types and state that type 4 had not been found at the time.
directed.conceptual_reading: Classification depends on how the continuous zero configuration is discretized by Gram intervals and sampled boundaries. A small observational perturbation can reclassify an event without changing the underlying zeros, making cross-program agreement a useful but local robustness check.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Zero-count patterns inside Gram blocks bridge analytic zero locations to discrete exception types. Exact Gram-point sampling and shifted sampling are two observation maps; comparing them exposes which reported categories may be unstable.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The flattened OCR table does not safely define all six types, so only the prose-stated reclassification and occurrence claims are usable. Failure to observe type 4 is not proof of impossibility, and agreement on one finite overlap does not exclude misses elsewhere.
directed.uncertainty: High confidence in the detection-bias mechanism and local agreement claim; low confidence in exact table geometry, type definitions, and OCR-rendered indices without scan verification.
